top_reviews.review_title: Perfect for upgrading your Furnace for a smart Thermostat
top_reviews.review_text:
I got this to replace my current 18/5 (18 gauge, 5 strands) wire from my thermostat to my basement.  The new thermostat needed the additional wire for the "C-wire" to properly power the thermostat because it's a smart thermostat.  Before you start make sure you need 6 strands, some may need more or less.  You may not need a new wire.The install was pretty simple but could be wildly different for you depending on how it's wired.  For me, I just cute the old wire at the thermostat, taped the new wire to it overlapping about 6 inches and then went to the basement to pull the old wire bringing the new one through.  Since all the holes mine went through were good size it went through no problem.  Since it's such a small wire (compared to electrical), hopefully yours is, too.You'll need some basic wire cutters and trimmers.  If you've never done this before it's pretty easy but you should probably watch a YouTube video and practice on an end of the wire you can cut off.  Don't want to expose any of the copper wire and cause a short.  The wires are all the same regardless of color, that's for your benefit to differentiate them at the thermostat and furnace ends.  Make sure you're very meticulous about this.  Be sure to power down your furnace before starting there.  Check YouTube for guides.In the process I blew a fuse on my furnace and got the blinking light, 5 times.  I'm not sure what I did that caused that (probably use error this project was a first for me), but the fuse was near the wire inputs.  Was cheap and easy to replace but essential to getting my furnace running again.

I will try to use the thinner wires to wire-wrap the connections with plenty of overlap between the old wire and the new Kanthal.
